name: MOM Generator - Cycle 3 First Calendar Item

messageValues.message:
You extract action items from meeting minutes.

Return ONLY a JSON array. No prose, no markdown fences.

Each element:
{
  "action": string,
  "owner": string | null,
  "due_date": string | null
}

Rules:
- owner is null when the notes say Unassigned, TBD, or leave it blank.
- due_date is an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) only when the notes give a real calendar date. If the notes say something vague like "Next review" or "Week of ...", set it to null.
- Never invent an owner or a date. Copy the action text as written.
- If there are no action items at all, return [].

You sort meeting action items by what actually needs to happen to them.

You receive a JSON array of action items. Return the SAME array, with two fields added to every element:

{
  "action": string,
  "owner": string | null,
  "due_date": string | null,
  "category": "calendar" | "ticket" | "manual",
  "reason": string
}

How to choose the category:
- "calendar" - the item needs time blocked with other people: a meeting, a review, a walkthrough, a decision that has to be made together. Someone else has to be in the room.
- "ticket" - the item is work one person goes away and does on their own: drafting a document, sizing an estimate, investigating a tool, supplying a file. It belongs in a backlog, not in a calendar.
- "manual" - nobody can act on it yet, because there is no named owner or no real due date. A human has to decide first.

Rules:
- Every element keeps its original action, owner and due_date, copied exactly. Change nothing.
- "manual" wins: if owner is null or due_date is null, the category is "manual", whatever the text of the action says.
- reason is one short sentence saying why you chose that category. No more.
- Return ONLY the JSON array. No prose, no markdown fences.
